items.q: What is a B2B market?
items.why: B2B means business to business, for example a firm that supplies packaging to food manufacturers.

items.q: Which is an example of a C2C market?
opts: A supermarket selling food to shoppers
A steel firm selling to a car maker
People selling second-hand clothes to each other on Vinted
A bank lending to a business
items.why: C2C is consumer to consumer, usually through a platform that takes a fee.

items.q: What is the difference between sales volume and sales value?
opts: Volume is the number of units sold; value is the money received from those sales
Volume is for goods; value is for services
Volume is in pounds; value is in units
items.why: Sales value = sales volume × price. They can move in different directions when price changes.

items.q: What does a strong negative correlation between two variables show?
opts: As one rises, the other falls, and the points lie close to a line
There is no link between them
One variable causes the other to fall
As one rises, the other rises
items.why: Negative means they move in opposite directions. Strong means the points are close to the line of best fit.

items.q: Ice cream sales and sunglasses sales are strongly positively correlated. What can you conclude?
opts: They tend to rise together, but this does not prove that one causes the other
Sunglasses cause ice cream sales to rise
Buying ice cream makes people buy sunglasses
items.why: Correlation shows a link, not a cause. Here both are probably caused by a third factor: hot, sunny weather.

items.q: A product has a PED of -0.4. Which word describes its demand?
items.why: The PED is between 0 and -1, so quantity demanded changes by a smaller percentage than price.

items.q: Demand for a product is price elastic. The business raises its price. What happens to revenue?
items.why: Quantity falls by a larger percentage than price rises, so revenue falls.

items.q: Which of these is most likely to make demand more price elastic?
opts: It is a small part of customers' spending
items.why: If customers can easily switch to a similar product, they react more to price changes.

items.q: What sign does the YED of an inferior good have?
items.why: For an inferior good, demand falls when income rises, so YED is negative.

items.q: Products with a YED greater than +1 are often described as what?
items.why: Demand rises by a bigger percentage than income, as with foreign holidays or eating out.

items.q: What is psychographic segmentation based on?
items.why: Psychographic segmentation groups customers by how they live and what they care about, for example people who value sustainability.

items.q: Which is an example of behavioural segmentation?
opts: Grouping customers by how often they buy and how loyal they are
items.why: Behavioural segmentation looks at what customers do: usage rate, loyalty, occasion of purchase.

items.q: What is one advantage of operating in a niche market?
opts: A very large number of potential customers
Less competition, so the business may be able to charge a higher price
items.why: Niche markets are small, so big firms may ignore them. A business that meets the niche's needs well can often charge more.

items.q: What is one disadvantage of operating in a mass market?
opts: Strong competition, which can push prices and margins down
items.why: Mass markets attract large rivals, so it is hard to stand out and there is often pressure to cut prices.

items.q: What does conversion mean as a marketing objective?
opts: Changing the product into a new version
Moving customers from one product to another
The percentage of potential customers who take an action, such as buying, after seeing marketing or visiting a site
items.why: A conversion objective might be to raise the share of website visitors who buy from 2% to 3%.

items.q: What is lead generation?
opts: Setting the leading price in the market
Finding potential customers who have shown interest in the product
items.why: Leads are people who might buy, for example by signing up for emails or asking for a quote. They can then be turned into customers.

items.q: What does customer retention mean?
opts: Holding stock until customers want it
Keeping existing customers buying from the business
items.why: It is usually cheaper to keep a customer than to win a new one.

items.q: Which is an example of seasonal demand?
opts: Sales rising because of a new advert
Sales of garden furniture rising every spring and summer
items.why: Seasonal demand follows the time of year. Cyclical demand follows the economy.

items.q: Which of these is an influence on the size of a marketing budget?
opts: The legal form of the business only
How much finance the business has available
items.why: The budget depends on things like available finance, the marketing objectives, what rivals spend and the stage of the product's life cycle.

items.q: A business wants to sell more to a new target market. What should it do to its marketing mix?
opts: Adapt it to suit that market, for example its price, where it sells and how it promotes the product
items.why: Different target markets have different needs and habits, so the mix usually needs adapting.
